The container/OPF pair is read with linear-time regexes rather than an XML parser: `xml.etree.ElementTree` is explicitly not safe against hostile input, all that is needed from it is three attributes, and `defusedxml` would be a new dependency for the one format we just declined to take one for. Those regexes tolerate two legal OPF spellings that a spec-shaped reading would have missed — attribute values in single quotes, and OPF elements carrying a namespace prefix (`<opf:item>`) — because getting either wrong fails **silently**: the spine is dropped, extraction falls back to archive order, and the chapters come back in an arbitrary sequence with nothing in the output saying so. Both are pinned by a test whose fixture puts archive order and spine order in deliberate disagreement, since a single-chapter fixture cannot tell the two paths apart. A corrupt archive still rejects, with a message that says the archive is the problem and that no extra or image variant changes it.

- A contract test pins the upload allowlist against the extraction story, so a future allowlist entry with no reader fails a test instead of quietly becoming another accepted-then-rejected upload.

- Keboola sliced exports on Azure-backed stacks now download through the legacy SDK client path (incremental + partitioned syncs). That path carried its own scheme chain which handled `gs://` and `s3://` but had no `azure://` arm, so an Azure slice reached `requests` as a raw `azure://` URI and failed the same way AWS slices did before the `s3://` fix ("No connection adapters were found"). Both paths now share one dispatch.

- A sliced-export URI in a scheme this build does not handle is refused where the manifest is read, naming the scheme, instead of being passed through as if it were an already-signed URL and failing several layers down.

- Gzip detection on the legacy SDK client's sliced-download path is now query-aware: it inspects the URL's last path segment instead of the full URL. A presigned HTTPS slice URL carries a query string after the `.gz` name (S3 signature, Azure SAS), and the shared `gs://` rewrite above appends `?alt=media`, so the old `endswith(".gz")` check never matched and gzipped slice bytes were written raw into the CSV. The primary path already checked the path segment; both now share one detector.

- **An instance with more than 200 Collections no longer hides the tail — including from its own access check.** `file_corpora_repo().list()` defaults to `limit=200` on both backends, and six callers read it meaning "every live corpus". The worst of them was an authorization *input*: `accessible_collection_ids` builds the owned half of a caller's reachable set from that list, so past 200 rows the owner of a Collection was told they could not reach it — a truncation that fails **closed** and reads as "the grant is broken" rather than "the list was cut off". The same cap silently trimmed `GET /api/collections` and the search surface's accessible-id set (no pagination signal to the caller), the `/agents` builder's knowledge-source picker, the id→name map behind the knowledge-artifact listing, and the corpora enumerated for knowledge packaging — so a Collection past the cap was also never packaged. The five that genuinely need every row now call a new unbounded `list_all()`, added to the DuckDB and Postgres repositories together and covered by the cross-engine contract test, mirroring `table_registry.list_all()`. The access check instead uses the `created_by` SQL predicate with an explicit high cap, so the fix does not put a whole-table read on the authorization path — the same reasoning `_owned_collection_ids` already applies in `src/agent_scope_intersection.py`. `app/resource_types.py` was already explicit about this with `_GRANT_PROJECTION_LIMIT` and is unchanged.

- **`agnes agent list`/`show`/`schedule list` now work with a plain PAT — including the default `agnes login` token — not just a fresh interactive session.** Every `/api/v1/agents*` route ran through `require_session_token`, which rejects every PAT flavor outright — so a normally-logged-in analyst holding only a PAT (no fresh browser session) could never even list their own agents, even though `agnes chat`'s own error text points them at `agnes agent list` for discovery. Three READ-only routes (`GET /api/v1/agents`, `GET /api/v1/agents/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/agents/{slug}/schedules`) now accept both a full-surface PAT and a `surface='stack'`-narrowed PAT — the `agnes login`/`agnes init` default — since that surface narrows *data reads* only, never the caller's own agent metadata. `GET /api/v1/agents/{id}/memories` stays on the more conservative full-surface-PAT-or-session rule (a memory notebook can hold free-text content, the most sensitive of the four read surfaces). New `require_session_or_user_pat` dependency factory (`app/auth/dependencies.py`); every mutating route (create/update/delete/scope/token issuance/memory writes) stays session-token-only regardless of PAT surface. An agent-scoped PAT is still denied everywhere. Also closes a pre-existing surface-check bypass on these same four reads: the check only fired for `typ="pat"`-shaped credentials, so a chat-sandbox token (`mint_session_jwt`, no `typ` claim) or an MCP-OAuth connector token — both also stamped `credential_surface="stack"` — reached `memories` unchecked; the surface rule now applies to any credential carrying that tag, regardless of `typ`.

- **Keboola local/remote sync no longer risks extracting with the wrong project's token.** Only the materialized pass resolved a per-`connection_id` Keboola credential; the extractor subprocess that handles `local`/`remote` registry rows always used a single global `KEBOOLA_STACK_URL`/`KEBOOLA_STORAGE_TOKEN` pair, so a UI-created connection's rows never synced and, on a multi-connection instance, a second project's rows could silently extract with the first project's token. The extractor pass now groups rows by `connection_id` and resolves each group's own credential (vault first, then the connection's `token_env`) via the same resolution `_run_materialized_pass` already used — extracted into a shared helper. A row whose connection has no resolvable credential is recorded as `sync_state` error `missing_connection_token` and skipped, never silently synced with the wrong token. Rows with no `connection_id` are unaffected. Because every group writes the same `extracts/keboola/extract.duckdb` and the extractor's default mode rebuilds it from scratch, groups after the first now run in merge mode — seeding the build from the current extract and replacing only their own tables — so a pass with several connections keeps every group's tables instead of only the last one's; the global group is dispatched first, running fresh to preserve the whole-pass prune semantics and keeping first-writer ownership of the `kbc` `_remote_attach` alias.

- **Sync status no longer disagrees with itself across admin pages.** `sync_state.table_id` was written keyed by a table's registry *name* while `/admin/data-sources`'s pipeline strip and the Tables lens' delivery map joined it against `table_registry` on *id* — so a table registered with a display name that isn't already a valid identifier (spaces, uppercase — e.g. `"Web Sessions"`, id `web_sessions`) showed healthy sync status on one admin surface and "never synced" on another, from the exact same sync. Writers (`app/api/sync.py`'s materialized pass, the orchestrator's rebuild + filesystem-fallback paths) now resolve the registry id at write time (`src/sync_state_key.py`), `/api/admin/registry`'s join tries id first, and a one-time backfill migration (schema v123) rewrites existing name-keyed rows. `/admin/tables` also gains a Sync column (status pill + relative time) — previously the sync state existed only on `/admin/sync`.

- **`PUT /api/admin/registry/{id}` now rejects a rename that collides with another table's name or id** (409), mirroring the check `POST /api/admin/register-table` already ran. `table_registry.name` has no database-level uniqueness constraint, and the id-first sync_state/manifest resolvers this same change introduces (`_reg_for` in `app/api/sync.py`, the distribution mirror job, `list_registry`) would otherwise misroute a legacy name-keyed `sync_state` row to the wrong table after an unchecked rename.

- **`/api/query` no longer lets a caller read absolute parquet paths out of DuckDB's SQLite-compat catalog.** The SELECT-only guard already blocked DuckDB's own metadata surfaces (`duckdb_views`, `information_schema`, …), but not the SQLite-compat aliases DuckDB also answers — `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master` (and `sqlite_schema` / `sqlite_temp_master` / `sqlite_temp_schema`) returns every view's full `CREATE VIEW` body, which for the orchestrator's master views is `... AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('/data/extracts/<source>/data/<id>.parquet')` — disclosing the server's absolute on-disk layout to any query caller regardless of RBAC. `duckdb_external_file_cache()` leaked the same paths directly. All five are now on the blocklist, in both the `/api/query` guard (`app/api/query.py`) and the hybrid/remote engine's sibling list (`src/remote_query.py`), which execute against the same local DuckDB views. BigQuery's `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` stays allowed — it runs remotely and discloses nothing local.

- **The single-VM TLS proxy no longer exposes `GET /metrics` publicly.** The Prometheus endpoint is unauthenticated by design — internal-scrape-only, with docs/observability.md instructing operators never to expose it — and the mtier proxy has denied it at the edge since it shipped, but the root `Caddyfile` (every `tls_mode=caddy` deployment) forwarded it to the app along with everything else, publishing queue depth, worker-lane occupancy, replica `hostname:pid`, per-route latency histograms, and the full route inventory to anyone who could reach the instance's HTTPS port. The primary site block now answers `/metrics` with the same 404 the mtier proxy uses; `/healthz` + `/readyz` stay reachable (status-only, double as uptime probes), and scrapers keep polling the app port from inside the deployment boundary as documented. Running VMs pick the change up on the next config refresh — no image release required.

- **A semantic model created, edited, or deleted through the admin API now stays in sync with `metric_definitions`/`glossary_terms`/`column_metadata`, instead of projecting once and then rotting or leaking.** `POST`/`PUT /api/admin/semantic-models` only wrote the raw Ossie document — the flat-table projection that `agnes catalog --metrics`, chat metric lookups and search all read ran only for a synced source (git/upload/connection), so a hand-authored model's metrics never showed up anywhere. Both endpoints now call the same `project_document` the source importer uses, scoped (`partial=True`) to just that model's own id prefix — every `source='manual'` row shares one provenance tuple, so an unscoped prune would otherwise delete a *sibling* manual model's rows on every unrelated write. `DELETE /api/admin/semantic-models/{id}` now prunes those same three tables (`prune_model`, reusing the identical model-id-prefix scoping) before removing the document row, so deleting a model no longer leaves its metrics/glossary/columns orphaned. `agnes admin semantic-model import` rides the same endpoint and now projects too.

- **`agnes schema` / `/api/v2/schema` carry real per-column descriptions instead of a hardcoded blank — filtered to the caller's own semantic-model access.** All three local schema-building branches (BigQuery, internal, local-parquet) always returned `"description": ""`, even when a description existed in admin-authored `column_metadata` or in a bound semantic-model dataset field. Descriptions are now resolved with `column_metadata` (unscoped, same boundary as table access) taking precedence over an Ossie dataset field description bound to the same table — the latter filtered per-request through the caller's own semantic-model read access (`ResourceType.SEMANTIC_MODEL`, strictly narrower than table access) and never baked into the shared schema cache, so a caller without access to a model never sees text from it, and an earlier caller's cache-warming request can never leak that model's text to a later, less-privileged caller. `""` when neither source has one.

- **A semantic model's browse page now says when metrics were dropped for an unsupported dialect, instead of showing nothing.** A metric declared only in a warehouse-specific dialect (e.g. SNOWFLAKE-only, no ANSI_SQL/DuckDB fallback) is silently skipped at projection; `/semantic-layer/{slug}` now shows a "N metrics skipped (unsupported dialect)" warning pill next to the model's status badges.

### Removed

- **`.msg` (Outlook) no longer passes the upload allowlist**, and an upload containing one is refused in the response (**422**, `unsupported_type`) instead of accepted with **201** and rejected by the background task a minute later. Nothing has changed about what the product could actually do with such a file: no extractor read it on any build, including the `-rich` image, so the only thing the old acceptance bought an uploader was a delayed failure and an invitation to retry — the one action that could not help. Other files in the same batch are still stored and indexed normally; only the response status changes. Re-adding it means a parser first, and the only real option — `extract-msg` — resolves to 15 transitive packages, among them a Tkinter GUI toolkit and two VBA/malware-analysis tools, so it belongs behind an opt-in extra rather than in every image; the reasoning is recorded next to the allowlist so the decision does not have to be rediscovered. Exporting the mail as `.eml` is read by the standard library on every build.

- **`scripts/bench_retrieval.py` — measures Collections retrieval past its documented design point, with a capacity answer rather than a guess.** `src/ingest/retrieval.py` says what it is ("brute-force at the current scale (dozens of files)"): every `search()` fetches every chunk of the caller's granted corpora into Python and scores them there. The script seeds a synthetic corpus at chosen scales and reports p50/p95 for the fetch phase, the rank phase and the total, plus peak RSS — because the likelier wall here is memory, not milliseconds: `_SELECT` includes `embedding FLOAT[384]`, so every candidate's 384 floats are materialized on **every** query, including on a deployment with no embedding model where nothing reads them. Measured on one laptop, 6 queries per scale, lexical-only: **25k chunks → 456 ms p50 / 371 MB**, **100k → 1.86 s p50 / 920 MB**, **240k → 4.79 s p50, 5.12 s p95 / 1.8 GB**. Cost is linear in corpus size, as the brute-force loop implies. With vectors present the same 25k corpus costs **1.72 s p50 / 842 MB** — ~3.8× the time and ~2.3× the memory of the lexical path at equal chunk count. A `--embed` run injects a query vector so the cosine+fusion branch is measured without needing the heavy optional model installed. Guard tests (`tests/test_bench_retrieval_harness.py`) pin the harness to the production column list and assert the embedded run really reaches the cosine path, so the numbers cannot quietly start describing something else.

### Internal

- **The test suite stops rebuilding the FastAPI app once per test.** `create_app()` measured ~430 ms (roughly 90 `include_router` calls plus middleware), and the suite has built it once per session since the `_shared_seeded_app` fixture landed — but 74 test files had drifted back to rolling their own function-scoped app fixture, covering 1229 tests. A random 60-file sample spent 83% of its wall-clock in fixture setup and ~71% of that in per-test `create_app()`. Those files now request the new session-shared `shared_app` fixture; the same 1455 tests went from 104 s to 59 s *while halving the worker count*. Isolation is unchanged — repos read `DATA_DIR` at call time, so a fixture that still redirects it per test keeps its own state — and `tests/test_shared_app_contract.py` is the ratchet that keeps the pattern from drifting back, with an allowlist for the two fixtures that genuinely need a private app (lifespan tests, and the dual-backend `seeded_app_both`).

- **`-n auto` no longer means "one worker per core" on a developer machine.** Each xdist worker is a full Python process that imports `app.main`, measured at ~430 MB RSS once warm; on a 14-core laptop `-n auto` peaked at 6.5 GB across 15 processes for three test files, pinned every core on a suite that is mostly waiting on DuckDB file I/O, and made a second worktree's suite unrunnable. Local runs now cap what `auto` resolves to at 6 workers (same three files: 2.9 GB across 7 processes). The trade is explicit: across the whole suite this costs ~14% wall-clock for ~55% less RAM, so the default run is ~6% slower than before while using a third less CPU. `AGNES_TEST_MAX_WORKERS` overrides the cap and an explicit `-n N` is untouched; CI is exempt, since its runners have few cores and shard wall-clock is the thing being tuned.

- **`tests/db_pg` boots one Postgres per RUN instead of one per xdist worker.** `_pg_url` is session-scoped, but under xdist every worker runs its own session, so each called `mkdtemp()` and got a private server: `-n auto` meant one full postmaster and a 300-640 MB data dir per core (8 concurrent instances observed from consecutive owner PIDs). pgserver already refcounts holders of a data dir across processes behind an interprocess lock — it was simply never given the same path twice. Keying the data dir on xdist's `testrun_uid` collapses N servers into one, with each worker isolated in its own *database* on it (a stronger boundary than the per-worker `public` schema it replaces). A four-worker run drops from four servers to one, 290 MB total. Fixtures that deliberately need a private, untouched server keep it through the explicit `_start_dedicated_pgserver` helper.

- **Leaked test scratch is swept at every session start, not only when `tests/db_pg` runs.** The orphaned-pgserver reaper lived in the PG package's own session fixture, so a developer who never invoked that package accumulated orphans indefinitely — 10 dirs totalling 4.1 GB on one machine. It now runs from the root `pytest_sessionstart` for every invocation, alongside a new sweep of stale `.agnes-test-data*` roots (24 h floor, so a concurrent worktree's live root is never touched). The reaper's minimum-age guard also no longer outranks its own evidence: a dir whose owner sentinel names a dead PID is a proven orphan and is reaped immediately, where before it waited an hour — which is why all 10 of those dirs were under the threshold at once, a `-n auto` run creating them faster than they aged out.

- **Two git worktrees can run the suite at the same time.** The default `DATA_DIR` was `$TMPDIR/.agnes-test-data/<worker>`, with no per-checkout component, so `gw0` in one worktree and `gw0` in another resolved to the same `system.duckdb` — a real 18-35 MB file per worker, under DuckDB's exclusive file lock. The root is now keyed on a hash of the checkout path, matching the scheme the shared pgserver data dir uses.

- Sliced-export URI schemes are a declared closed set (`SliceScheme`) dispatched exhaustively via `typing.assert_never`, so a backend added without an arm is a type error rather than a runtime discovery. The legacy client's second scheme chain is gone; a guard fails if one reappears.

- Type checking now blocks over a curated "typed core" (`scripts/typecheck-core.sh`, driven by `tests/test_exhaustiveness_gate.py` so it rides the required `test` check). The repo-wide mypy step stays advisory — it never gated, and mypy was not installed locally either, so the post-edit hook skipped it silently and an `assert_never` would only have tripped if the missing arm was reached in production. mypy is now a declared `[dev]` dependency, the gate fails loudly rather than skipping in CI, and it self-tests by mutating a dispatch to confirm it still rejects one.

- The exhaustiveness gate guards its own call sites: a `# type: ignore` on an `assert_never`, or a file-wide `# mypy: ignore-errors` in a typed-core module, is refused. Both keep the typed core mypy-clean while enforcing nothing, and neither was visible to the other checks.

- `tests/test_keboola_client_gcs_slice.py` asserted the divergence between the two `gs://` rewrites rather than a contract; it now covers the shared rewrite. The legacy path's GCS slice URL changes to the JSON-API media form already used on the primary path.

## [0.85.1] - 2026-08-24

### Added

- **`AGNES_CHAT_PROVIDER` env override + per-VM `chat_provider` module field — pin the web-chat provider in infrastructure.** `chat.provider` now resolves env > `instance.yaml` > `e2b` (the standard precedence every other chat env override follows), and the `customer-instance` module gains a per-VM `chat_provider` field (`""` default = no env line; values validated against the app's own boot allowlist at plan time, and `"kai-agent"` requires `kai_agent_enabled` on the same VM). Codifies the provider choice in code-reviewed Terraform instead of a hand-edited `instance.yaml` overlay on the data disk — the overlay survives reboots and VM recreates, but not a fresh data disk, and it is invisible in review.

## [0.85.0] - 2026-08-23

### Added

- **Retiring a marketplace plugin is one action instead of a four-step dance.** `admin_disabled` hides a plugin from every served surface but deliberately keeps its `resource_grants` rows, and the group Access tab hides disabled plugins — so an admin who wanted a deprecated plugin *gone*, grants included, had to disable it, discover the grants still existed, re-enable it to make them editable, revoke per group, then disable it again, per instance. `POST /api/marketplaces/{id}/plugins/{name}/disable` now takes an optional `{"revoke_grants": true}` body that deletes every `marketplace_plugin` grant on that plugin in the same call and reports the count as `revoked_grants`; the Details-modal disable dialog grows a matching opt-in checkbox and the success toast names the number revoked. Plain disable is unchanged — no body, grants preserved, re-enable restores the plugin for the same groups — because "temporarily pull it" and "retire it" are different intents and only the second one should be destructive.

- **`agnes admin marketplace` — the curated-marketplace admin surface is scriptable.** `list`, `sync <slug>`, `disable-plugin <marketplace>/<plugin> [--revoke-grants]`, `enable-plugin <marketplace>/<plugin>`, each `--json`-able. The disable/enable pair had no CLI analogue at all, so retiring a plugin across a fleet meant clicking through every instance's admin UI or hand-rolling curl with an admin PAT. Plugins are addressed by the same `<marketplace>/<plugin>` ref that `resource_grants.resource_id` uses, so a ref read out of a grant listing pastes straight in, and a malformed ref or unknown slug hints `agnes admin marketplace list` rather than failing bare. Marketplace registration/deletion stay web-UI-only on purpose (they carry a git token), and the disable/enable pair stays deliberately un-exposed to MCP: an agent-invokable instance-wide kill switch over served plugins is a privilege-escalation seam, not a convenience.

- **Curator-side deprecation: `"deprecated": true` in `marketplace-metadata.json` retires a plugin fleet-wide.** Until now the format had no lifecycle field at all, so "this plugin is deprecated, never use it" lived only in people's heads and in per-instance admin clicks — a curator could delete the plugin from the repo (breaking anyone pinned to it) or ask every instance admin to disable it by hand. A plugin section carrying the literal boolean `true` (plus optional single-line `deprecation_note` and `replacement`) is now admin-disabled automatically right after each sync's plugin-cache write, so one upstream commit takes it off every consuming instance. Strictly the literal boolean — `"true"`, `1` or a list is rejected with a warning, because a typo must never retire a plugin. One-way by design: removing the flag later never auto-re-enables, and re-enabling a still-flagged plugin lasts until the next sync re-disables it, so the admin stays the one who decides whether a retired plugin comes back. `GET /api/marketplaces/{id}/plugins` surfaces the three fields (read on demand from the cloned tree, like the rich detail-page content) and the Details modal renders a DEPRECATED pill carrying the curator's note and replacement. Grants are untouched — pair the flag with the retirement checkbox above when they should go too. Plain Claude Code consumers of the same repo ignore the metadata file entirely, so the field degrades gracefully outside Agnes.

### Fixed

- **An agent built in `/agents` now enforces the scope the page shows, instead of running with its owner's entire stack.** The builder wrote its Knowledge and Capabilities picks to the `knowledge`/`plugins` columns only, leaving all four `*_mode` columns at the repository default `'all'` — the passthrough shape, which skips the scope intersection entirely. So an agent presented as grounded in one data package could read every table, memory domain and collection its owner could, and the UI's narrowing was decoration. `POST`/`PATCH /api/agents` now derive `agent_scope` rows from the declaration and set the four modes to `'selected'`, so the runtime enforces it: the broker mints an agent-session identity and every brokered read is authorized against (owner grants ∩ declared scope). A rename does not touch scope; editing the declaration replaces only the builder-owned rows, so a Slack channel binding or a CLI-set table/connection row survives. Two knock-on effects worth knowing: a builder agent can now be **issued a PAT** (issuance requires all four modes `'selected'`, so builder agents were API-unreachable by construction), and an agent whose declaration is empty now reaches nothing rather than everything. The builder's read projection hydrates `knowledge`/`plugins` from the stored `agent_scope` rows when those columns are empty, so a governance-created agent — one scoped through `agnes agent scope set`, which never writes the JSON columns — shows its real scope instead of "0 sources · 0 tools"; without that, the first declaration edit wiped all four builder-owned axes with the user never having seen what they were destroying. The write half matches: a PATCH carrying only one axis derives the other from that same hydrated view rather than from the raw JSON columns, so a partial save cannot drop the half it did not send. Listing is one batched scope read for the whole page rather than one per agent (`get_scope_for_agents`, added on both backends with a contract test).

- **Editing a builder declaration also stops the connection axis passing through, which is a narrowing worth planning for.** `rescope` forces all four `*_mode` columns to `'selected'`, `connections_mode` included — the builder has no connections section, and an axis the UI never offers must not silently pass the owner's whole MCP surface through while the page claims the agent is scoped. The consequence: an agent still at the all-`'all'` passthrough default that is edited in the builder narrows to its *declared* connection rows, usually none, so it loses MCP connections it was implicitly reaching. Fail-closed on purpose, and recoverable — `agnes agent scope set --connection <id>` now takes effect immediately, since the mode is already `'selected'`. The v122 backfill does **not** do this to agents whose modes were deliberately set: its cohort is rows still at all-`'all'`, excluding the seeded default agent.
- **A declared data package confers the tables in it, and an owner's package-shaped access reaches their agents.** `tables_mode` governs the whole data axis — `table`, `data_package` and `collection` — because packages and collections are what the builder actually declares. A declared package is expanded to its member tables live per request, so a package edit reaches every agent scoped to it with no re-save. On the owner side, the intersection previously read `resource_grants(resource_type='table')` only, while the platform routes analyst table access through data packages: an agent whose owner held tables via a package was denied every one of them, with the catalog still listing them (`403 not in your stack` from inside the agent's own sandbox). Owner reach now also counts member tables of the owner's granted packages, plus collections the owner created — both without the admin god-mode short-circuit, so an admin-owned agent still gets only what was explicitly granted. `agnes agent scope set` gains `--data-package` and `--collection`, and `PUT /api/v1/agents/{id}/scope` accepts both item types, so the governance API and the builder describe one scope model rather than two.
- **The owner side of the data axis is bounded by the owner's effective stack, not just their grants.** A table read is authorized against `StackResolver.stack`, whose classic formula (`features.stack_auto_membership: false`) is `required ∪ (subscribed ∩ available)` — so an *available* package the owner never subscribed to is not in their stack and its tables are refused to them. Deriving the owner's packages from raw grants alone would have handed exactly those tables to their agent: strictly more than the owner has. The owner's package set is now bounded on both sides — `⊆` raw grants (so an admin owner still contributes only explicit grants, never the god-mode short-circuit or an ungranted self-subscription the resolver surfaces) and `⊆` effective stack — which is the only set that cannot exceed the owner on either axis.
- Schema v122 backfills the same enforcement onto builder agents created before this fix: their declaration becomes `agent_scope` rows and the modes flip off passthrough. The seeded default agent (web chat's own attribution row) and any agent whose scope was already set deliberately are left alone.
- The intersection is computed on every brokered request, so two costs on that path went with it: the owner's data-package set is resolved once per call instead of once per axis that needs it (a grant read plus a `StackResolver` pass, three times over), and the owner's own collections are filtered by `created_by` in SQL rather than by reading the table under a 100k cap and filtering in Python. `file_corpora_repo().list()` gains the predicate on both backends, contract-tested.

## [0.84.9] - 2026-08-23

### Fixed

- **Admin-disabling a plugin now removes it from every user-facing curated surface, as the confirmation dialog always promised.** The served feed, browse listing, my-stack and v2 `/skills` already filtered `marketplace_plugins.admin_disabled`, but three surfaces kept honoring a caller's still-live `resource_grants` row: the Library page listed the disabled plugin with a working "+ Add to stack" button, the curated detail page (and its inner skill/agent pages and served docs) still rendered, and `POST …/install` happily subscribed the caller — so operators had to revoke grants as a workaround, which "disabled" was specifically designed not to require. All of these now treat a disabled plugin as nonexistent (404, hidden in the Library), for admins too; the one surface that still shows it is the `/admin/marketplaces` Details modal, which carries the re-enable control. The two cover-art paths (`…/asset/`, `…/mirrored/`) are a deliberate exception and keep serving: both are login-only with no per-plugin RBAC because the content is marketing visuals with no PII/source/secrets, so a disable check would hide nothing a caller could not already fetch, while putting one serialized DuckDB round-trip per image back on a render-blocking path (12-20 covers per grid) those endpoints were explicitly stripped of DB work for — reasoning pinned in a test rather than left as an oversight. Grants are untouched and everything comes back on re-enable, exactly per docs/marketplace.md.

- **A synced table whose registry `id` differs from its `name` no longer previews as "no synced data yet".** The sync keys the parquet filename by the registry **name** (`_run_materialized_pass` convention; the extractors' `tc["name"]`), while `/api/v2/sample`, `/api/v2/schema` and `/api/v2/scan` looked the file up by the **id** off the request path. The register handler slugifies the id from the name (lower + spaces→underscores), so any wizard registration where the two differ — e.g. an uppercase source-table name — had its parquet written under a filename the read surfaces never checked: preview reported "the first sync is pending or failing" for a fully-synced table (queries were unaffected — DuckDB view names are case-insensitive). The resolver now tries the row's `name` first and the id as a fallback, and the 404 detail's last-sync-error lookup follows the same name-first convention, since `sync_state` is keyed by name too. The catalog's `rough_size_hint` follows it as well — `local_parquet_size_bytes` is the resolver's size counterpart, and keyed by id alone it published a null size for the very rows the read surfaces had just been taught to serve.

- **`/catalog/semantics` claimed there was no semantic layer when there was one.** Two pages carry the title "Semantic layer": `/catalog/semantics` renders the flat `metric_definitions` + `glossary_terms` projection, and `/semantic-layer` browses the stored Ossie document. Nothing on the former — the more reachable of the two, linked from the Library's Definitions block — pointed at the latter, so an instance whose document declares datasets and relationships but no aggregations rendered "No metrics registered yet. Import a starter pack with…" and read as an empty instance. Zero metrics is the *default* state of an imported document, not a sign the import failed. The page now offers a "Browse the full semantic layer" link in its header and names the document in the metrics empty state beside (not instead of) the import hint. Gated on the same `_can_read_model` tier the browse pages apply — a readable document, never this page's own counts — so a caller with no readable model is not sent to an empty page. `/library`'s footer already gated on exactly this condition with its own inline copy of the check; both surfaces now share one reader (`_has_readable_semantic_model`), since the two disagreeing is how the standalone page came to contradict the Library next door.

### Internal

- **`.test_durations` refreshed on CI hardware — 908 more tests now carry a measured duration (20,369 → 21,277).** pytest-split balances the 8 shards off this file and assigns an unmeasured test blind, so the file going stale is how one shard drifts minutes past another. Carried here rather than merged from its own automated PR (#1509): workflows do not run for a PR opened by `github-actions[bot]`, so that PR had **zero** checks against it and could never reach green — the generated split would have landed unverified. Riding a real train gives it a full CI round.

## [0.84.8] - 2026-08-22

### Added

- **`chat.provider: kai-agent` — web chat on the embedded kai-agent turn engine.** A third sandbox provider next to `e2b` and `docker`: sessions run on the embedded engine the `/api/kai/*` host wiring already serves (its own agent loop, transcript store and remote sandbox), so Agnes spawns nothing per session. The provider (`app/chat/kai_engine_provider.py`) translates the engine's SSE turn stream into the runner frame protocol the chat stack already speaks — history, mid-turn reconnect replay, message-rate limits, the concurrency cap and the web approval card all behave as with the native providers, with zero frontend changes. Sessions authenticate with a host-minted engine session JWT (`mint_engine_session_token`, the `POST /api/kai/sessions` claim contract extracted so the two cannot drift) and are created with UUID ids on both creation paths, web and the Slack producer (the engine's chat key is a uuid column). Cancel maps to the engine's stop endpoint, approval decisions to its approval endpoint (`chat.approvals_enabled: false` auto-denies, matching the native kill-switch), and pause/resume is pure bookkeeping — the manager also skips the native ticket mint/revoke pair for this provider, so a resume never 401s the engine's in-flight turn. Boot-gated on `KAI_HOST_JWT_SECRET`; the engine's address is `chat.kai_agent_url` (default `http://kai-agent:3000`). Stated limitations (docs/cloud-chat.md → "kai-agent provider (embedded turn engine)"): the engine stream carries no token usage, so `daily_anthropic_spend_usd`/`max_session_tokens` do not meter engine sessions; per-session personas (agent profiles/memories, co-drive grant intersection) do not reach the engine — and the two narrowed session kinds fail closed rather than widening to the owner, so a co-drive turn on this provider reaches no Agnes tool surface at all (`403 mcp_not_available_to_co_session`) instead of running unscoped; `per_tool_call_seconds`/`tool_calls_per_turn_budget` are inert; single-gateway only.

- **Both session forks honour a caller-owned id, so co-drive works on the engine provider.** `chat.provider: kai-agent` needs every session id to be a uuid, and `ChatManager.create_session` plus the Slack twin thread one in — but a fork is a session creator too. `fork_session_as_co_session` and `fork_co_session_to_private` minted `chat_<hex>` unconditionally, on **both** backends, so on an engine instance a brand-new co-drive session could never spawn and the error card told the user their seconds-old conversation "predates" the provider — advice that produced another dead one. Both forks now take an optional `session_id`, the co-presence endpoints pass the same decision, and the dead-handle copy no longer asserts a cause the handle cannot know. Contract-tested on both backends.

- **`daily_anthropic_spend_usd` and `max_session_tokens` no longer go silently inert.** Both are enforced off `chat_messages.tokens_in/out`, which only a usage-carrying frame writes; the engine's stream carries none. Both ship live defaults ($20/day, 200k/session), so switching provider removed two budgets instance-wide with nothing in the log or `/admin`. Boot now warns per configured cap and `GET /api/chat/readiness` reports them as `unmetered_caps`. Per-agent `token_budget_monthly` still applies — the broker enforces it on the engine's `llm` ticket.

- **The public agent API refuses on this provider instead of answering with the wrong persona.** `POST /api/v1/agents/{slug}/sessions` delivers an agent's system prompt, tone, greeting and memories by materializing them into the session workspace, which a self-credentialed provider never reads — so the caller got the instance template persona under the agent's name, and a narrowed-scope agent 403'd on every tool call. Now `503 agent_sessions_unavailable_on_provider`, refused before the session row is created.

- A refused engine Stop is logged instead of read as success (the turn used to hang with the composer locked until the SSE read timeout), and `/admin`'s chat banner labels `KAI_HOST_JWT_SECRET` instead of showing the raw payload key.

## [0.84.7] - 2026-08-21

### Added

- **`customer-instance` module: per-VM `kai_agent_broker_mcp_enabled` flag — give the embedded kai-agent engine's sandbox this instance's own MCP tool surface.** One flag renders both halves of a pair that only works together: the app-side ticket-scope switch (`KAI_BROKER_MCP_ENABLED=true` in the VM's app `.env`, which makes `/api/kai/tickets` issue the `kai_mcp` scope and unlocks `POST /api/kai/mcp`) and the engine-side broker URL (`HOST_BROKER_MCP_URL` derived from the VM's public origin, the same `SERVER_URL` the LLM broker line rides, because the E2B sandbox egresses to it from the public internet). Either half alone fails silently — the URL without the scope answers `503 kai_mcp_not_enabled` on every tool call (`_require_mcp_surface` is declared ahead of the ticket dependency, so it decides before any credential is inspected), the scope without the URL never registers the tool server — which is why it is one flag and not two env keys. Per-VM like `kai_agent_enabled` itself (the flag hands the engine the caller's tool surface, so a dev-first enable must not widen prod), default `false`, inert without `kai_agent_enabled`, and overridable via `kai_agent_env` (the caller map is appended after the derived lines, and env_file gives later keys precedence).

## [0.84.6] - 2026-08-21

### Fixed

- **Creating a data package could not choose the tables that go in it** — from the Library's "+ Add → New data package" or from `/admin/data-packages`' "+ New package", the form collected a name, slug, description, status, category, icon, colour, cover image and group access, and then made an *empty* package. The tables it exists to hold were a second trip: open the package's own page, click Edit, tick them there. The two-level PROJECT › BUCKET picker was already built and already in this drawer — search, tri-state boxes, project headings resolved from `source_connections` so a heading is a name rather than a raw uuid — but `applyMode()` hid it on a create (`tablesField.hidden = !editing`) and `hydrateTables()` only ran in edit mode. The stated reason was that a package being created has no id to attach a table to, which is true and was never the obstacle: the group picks in the same form are collected before the id exists and written once `POST /api/admin/data-packages` answers. Ticks now ride the same collect-then-apply order, so the picker is offered in both modes and membership is written immediately after the create. No endpoint is new — the same `POST /{id}/tables` edit mode has always used. Grant failures and table failures are counted **separately** out to the caller (`onCreated(pkg, grantFailures, tableFailures)`), because one merged number would send an admin looking in the wrong place; `/admin/tables`' toast names each. Since the picker lives in the shared component, `/admin/data-packages` gains it in the same change — the gap was never Library-specific, it was every create.

## [0.84.5] - 2026-08-20

### Fixed

- **`agnes schema <table>` on a Snowflake `query_mode='remote'` row said "Table 'X' not found in the registry."** — on a table that is registered and answers `agnes query --remote` fine. `/api/v2/schema/{table_id}` has upstream branches for BigQuery remote and Databricks remote but never grew a Snowflake one, so a remote row fell through to the local-parquet branch, found no parquet (a remote row has none) and 404-ed. It now reads the column list from Snowflake's own `information_schema.columns` through the same ATTACH the query path uses, so what `agnes schema` reports and what a query can bind cannot drift apart. `sql_flavor` stays `duckdb` — unlike Databricks there is no per-query ship to the warehouse; the analyst queries the ATTACHed `sf` catalog. An instance with no Snowflake connection configured still answers 404, which is honest there.

### Changed

- **BREAKING (admin API): repointing a data source now names the tables it will break, and asks first.** `POST /api/admin/server-config` and `POST /api/admin/configure` previously applied any well-formed patch; a patch that changes a connection-identity leaf under `data_source.` while registrations of that source exist is now REFUSED until it is re-sent with `confirm_connection_change: true`. Any automation that repoints a configured source without that field will start getting 409s. The guard is deliberately narrow — tuning knobs in the same block, a leaf re-sent unchanged, and a source with no registrations are all unaffected, so first-time setup is unchanged. `POST /api/admin/server-config` answers **409 `connection_change_affects_registrations`** when a patch changes a *connection-identity* leaf under `data_source.<source>` — Snowflake's `account`/`database`/`warehouse`/`user`/`role`/`auth_type`/credential-pointer, BigQuery's `project`/`billing_project`/`location`, Databricks' `host`/`warehouse_id`/`catalog`/`token_env`, Keboola's `stack_url`/`token_env` — while registrations of that source exist. The body carries the changed coordinates, the affected-table count and a sample; `confirm_connection_change: true` applies it. `POST /api/admin/configure` (the setup wizard) is gated the same way — it writes the same block, so leaving it out would keep a second unguarded door open. All four surfaces that save a connection — instance settings, the Snowflake and Databricks branches of the Add-data wizard, and the setup flow — answer the refusal through one shared confirm-and-retry helper (`js/connection_repoint.js`), so the dialog reads the same wherever you hit it and none of them becomes a dead end. Tuning knobs in the same block (scan caps, timeouts, pool sizes) and first-time setup are unaffected, and a leaf re-sent at its own default (the wizards always write `auth_type` / `token_env`) is not a change.

  Why it earns a gate: a registration resolves its upstream against the instance's one connection per source, and the result is baked into the extract's `_remote_attach.url` and into each remote view's `sf."SCHEMA"."TABLE"`. Repointing invalidates every existing row of that source at once, and the failure is invisible from the operator's seat — remote reads fail at bind time deep inside a query, materialized syncs fail at COPY time, and `last_sync_status` keeps reporting the last *successful* run.

## [0.84.4] - 2026-08-20

### Fixed

- **The install prompt read as prompt injection to Claude Code's own classifier.** The rendered CLI setup guide (`/home` step 4, `app/web/setup_instructions.py`) told the agent things it had no business asserting on the reader's behalf: with a TLS trust block emitted it appended that the fallback chain "is documented and OK to use", and it instructed "never print the token" — text that pre-empts a safety judgement reads as written to defuse one, and a real install transcript quoted that reassurance back as the reason to distrust the prompt. The preamble now states brand, host and binary as one system without arguing for trust, and the token line says the steps use the file path rather than forbidding display. `scripts/dev/prompt_phrases.py` gains the five phrases so they cannot come back, and the bundled seed template is reworded to match — tier 2 of the banned-phrase guard is now enforced with no baseline for it. **Both install-prompt sources carry the hardening, not just the renderer**: which one a deployment serves is an operator setting (`resolve_prompt` honors the prompt's `source_mode`, and `'git'` binds to the IWT clone's copy of the template instead of the Python renderer), so the redirect cap and the two-signal token pre-check are applied to the seed template as well, with a guard asserting the pair rather than the banned-phrase tiers, which can only check that text is absent.

- **The setup guide's token pre-check told the agent to continue when nobody had signed in.** It keyed on `~/.config/agnes/token.json` alone — a file holding `{access_token, email}` and never a server, one per machine, so on a laptop signed in to a different Agnes deployment it exists and proves nothing. Keying on `config.yaml`'s `server:` key instead swapped one false positive for a worse one: `/cli/install.sh` writes that key at install time and prints "1. Sign in…" immediately after, so the ordinary fresh-install path matched and the agent was sent past a genuinely absent credential to fail three steps later inside `agnes init --token-file`. The check now requires **both** signals in one command, and anything else — including the short-circuit's empty output — stops and points at `/home` step 4.

- **The CLI wheel downloads no longer follow a redirect.** `curl -L` was retained deliberately so a hop is an explicit failure (exit 47) rather than a silent fetch from wherever the redirect points; `--max-redirs 0` is now on both wheel downloads in the rendered guide and on the `/cli/install.sh` copy.

- **`agnes auth login` printed the sign-in URL only when it could not open a browser.** On a host where the browser launch silently no-ops, the flow waited on a URL the user never saw. The URL is now printed unconditionally, with "(could not launch a browser automatically)" reserved for the case that actually happened. The pre-flight echo of a bare `/cli/auth/start` URL is gone — that address cannot complete the flow, so printing it invited a dead end.

- **The workspace template hard-coded an example host.** `config/agnes_workspace_template.txt` shipped `--server-url https://agnes.example.com` where `agnes init` substitutes `{server_url}`, so the rendered file named a server nobody runs.

## [0.84.3] - 2026-08-20

### Added

- **The chat composer recalls this conversation's own sent messages with ArrowUp/ArrowDown, shell-history style.** ArrowUp only starts recall once the caret is at the top of the draft, so normal multi-line cursor movement is unaffected; once browsing, Up/Down keep cycling regardless of caret position, including messages sent before the current page load (seeded from persisted history on open/reconnect). ArrowDown past the newest entry restores whatever was still being typed.

### Fixed

- **The chat composer's prompt recall could serve a co-drive peer's prompts to the session owner.** `chat.js` filters the ArrowUp history stack on `m.sender_email`, over rows from `GET /api/chat/sessions/{id}/messages` — an endpoint that did not serialize the field. `!m.sender_email` was therefore unconditionally true, the filter was dead code, and after any reload or `full_refresh` the owner's ArrowUp walked back through everyone's prompts. The same absence silently broke `renderMessage`'s peer-attribution badge, which disappeared from the transcript on every reload for the same reason. The endpoint now sends `sender_email`; it is already carried by the repository layer and already exposed to participants by `/api/chat/copresence`, and this route 404s for a non-owner before reaching the payload, so nothing new is disclosed. A guard pins the two halves together, because a source-grep test cannot tell "this code exists" from "this code does anything" — which is how the dead filter shipped green with a resolved review thread.

- **ArrowUp now leaves the caret at the end of the recalled prompt**, matching ArrowDown and the shell history this is modelled on. It used to park at position 0, the one place a reader recalling a prompt to edit its tail has to navigate away from; since browsing makes further Up/Down caret-independent, that bought nothing.

## [0.84.2] - 2026-08-20

### Changed

- **Every admin↔analyst crossing now carries its origin, so no crossing loses your place.** The seam between the governance tree (`/admin/*`) and the consumption tree (Library, `/catalog/*`) was crossed by links that forgot where you came from: the package workspace's *"View as analyst"* landed on the reading page whose back link pointed at the Library; the Simulate lens's *"Share it →"* landed on the package **index** with the person dropped; and coming back to `/admin/access` reset the filter, scope and tree. The `?from=` pattern the store pages proved (`?from=admin-moderation`) is now the general contract: **"Open analyst page →"** (renamed — the reader arrives as themselves, so the old label claimed a preview it never was) carries `?from=admin` and the reading page's back link becomes *"← Back to Admin: {package}"*; Simulate's stop rows land on the specific package with `?from=simulate&user=`, the page shows *"Fixing access for {person} — their groups: …"* with a one-click *"Re-check {person} →"* back into the same preview; the picked person rides the URL (`?user=` deep link in and out), and the Access workspace's working set (filter, scope) survives the round trip. Grant rows on `/admin/access` are links now — the page that decides "who gets what" can finally answer "what *is* that" in one click — and the rail keeps **Library** lit on `/catalog/*`, `/memory/d/*`, `/apps/detail/*` and `/marketplace/*`, which used to highlight nothing at all.
- **One vocabulary for access, everywhere humans read it.** The same grant tier wore four costumes — `available/required` (the API enum), *Optional/Automatic* (admin editors), *Required/Optional* (the Library's filter facet), *"Always downloaded (required)"* (detail pages) — so an admin explaining access to an analyst had to translate between surfaces. The human words are now **Automatic** (in members' stacks with no add — the tier the API spells `required`) and **Optional** everywhere: the Library facet (relabeled **Access**), the grid-card and stack-card badges, the plugin detail pill, the package/domain detail Availability notes, and `agnes stack browse`'s REQUIREMENT column (`--json` keeps the raw enum for scripts; the API, DB values and CLI flags are wire format and unchanged). Stack state keeps its own pair — **In stack / Not in stack yet** — and the ~30 title-case *"In Stack"/"Add to Stack"* pills normalized to sentence case to match the toolbar segment. The one word that meant two things is split: group-membership provenance now reads *"Auto-joined — everyone here is a member"* so **Automatic** only ever means the grant tier. Simulate's *Can use / Cannot use* stays — that's a verdict, not a tier, and its tier suffixes already spoke the standard words.
- **The Library's stack filter is a pressed toggle again — "In stack only", with its count on the button — and the Scope segment is retired.** The Catalog/Marketplace fold's three-way segment (All · Yours · Available to add) framed the Library as a shop and gave two filters tab-rank. Both narrowings are ordinary refinements now: **"In stack only"** rides the bar as the design system's pressed-state toggle (`.fbar-toggle`, count on the button, rendered only while flipping it would change the list), slicing on strict Stack membership — the same axis the `?stack=in_stack` deep link and the chat empty state count by, not the old ownership blend; your own uploads answer to the Owner facet — and "what could I add" is the Filter menu's **"Not in stack yet"** toggle (rendered only while something is actually addable, restated as a removable chip when applied). Nothing is hidden: every acquirable row still sits in the unfiltered list wearing its own "+ Add to stack" pill, and the retired browse pages keep their meaning — `/marketplace` and `/catalog` redirects still send `?scope=available`, which arrives with the availability filter applied, and `?scope=mine` presses "In stack only".
- **`/admin/tokens` speaks the platform's toolbar language instead of its own.** The Tokens tab stacked three rows of page-local chrome — STATUS pills, SORT BY pills with a direction hidden behind a second click, and a full-page-wide search with *Clear filters* stranded at its far end — directly under a count strip repeating the same four numbers, while the profile tokens section, /library and /stack had all moved to the shared `.fbar`. Folded to two objects: the count strip **is** the status filter now (each card a toggle, *Total* the way back, zero-count cards dimmed rather than dead ends), and owner search + one sort select (key *and* direction legible at rest, incl. the admin-only *Owner A–Z*) sit in the shared `.fbar`, with refinements restated as removable chips that carry *Clear filters* only while something is refined. Card-level fixes ride along: a token that was never used says **"Never used"** instead of the orphaned *"Last used —"*, meta text ellipsizes against the card's real edge instead of a fixed 420px cap that chopped *"Revoked 12 days ago"* mid-word beside half a page of whitespace, "Recently used"/"Expiring soonest" sorts pin never-used/never-expiring tokens to the bottom instead of the top, and every colour resolves through `--ds-*` tokens so the page holds in dark theme.
- **Admin nav renames, labels only: "Library" → "Content", "Flea submissions" → "Submissions".** The Maintain section named "Library" held marketplaces, store moderation and curation — nothing the analyst Library shows — and the collision was the first thing a new admin tripped on. Section keys and every URL are unchanged; "flea" leaves the labels per the authoring-seam spec's decision 8 (retire the word, not the URLs).

### Fixed

- **A paused admin no longer sees admin chrome that only leads to a 403.** Pausing elevation is a consent gate — `require_admin` refuses the request (403 `admin_elevation_paused`) and the admin runs on their explicit grants — but `session.user.is_admin` was raw Admin-group membership, so every admin affordance stayed on screen, the rail's Admin row first among them, and each one led to an error page. The flag is **effective authority** now (membership *and* not paused), so the chrome matches the authority the request actually has; a companion `is_admin_paused` carries the difference, and the rail spends the slot saying so — a muted *"Admin paused"* row linking to the switch — because silence reads as a bug ("where did Admin go?"). Nothing is stranded: that switch lives on `/me/profile`, which is deliberately not admin-gated, so pausing is always reversible. Enforcement paths are untouched (they call `is_user_admin` / `require_admin` directly); this pair is for rendering, and the new guard asserts on the rendered page that a paused admin is served no link into `/admin` at all.
- **Two Overview buttons stop naming a place and opening another.** *"Simulate a person →"* on the setup chain's last step carried `href="/admin/access"` — the Groups workspace, when Simulate is a sibling lens on that path (`?lens=simulate`) — so the one button whose whole promise is "see the instance exactly as their groups leave it" delivered the who-gets-what editor. Its done-state sibling had the same defect from the other direction: a step showed *"Bundle tables"* while open and *"Manage packages"* once done, but both states shared one `href`, so the maintenance label opened the Tables lens, a page about something else. Steps can now carry a `done_href` (defaulting to `href`, so nothing else moves) and the label and destination switch together. A structural guard checks every journey step whose CTA names a destination against **that state's own** href, so the next renamed lens or moved page fails a test rather than a click.
- **The Simulate lens stops painting dangling grants green.** A grant whose package had been deleted rendered through the can-use path as a green chip carrying a raw id — a false positive in the one lens built for compliance questions. It is now an explicit warning chip plus a stop row naming the group whose grant is stale, with *"Fix the grant →"* one click away. Tier joined the output at the same time: every package chip and chain row now says **Automatic — in their stack** or **Optional — must add it**, answering the question the pane's own lede promised ("membership to grant to *tier*") instead of stopping at "a grant exists".
- **The onboarding tour's Library step points at a control that exists again.** Its ring and fallback targeted `#lib-stack-toggle`, which the Scope segment replaced in the Catalog/Marketplace fold — on current builds the step silently fell through to nothing. Retargeted to `#lib-scope`, with the step copy naming the segment ("Yours") instead of the retired toggle.
- **The two analyst dead-ends answer with doors instead of machine tokens.** Data that exists but isn't shared used to render a raw `access_denied`; it now says *"Not shared with you yet — {package} exists, but isn't shared with any of your groups"* with a **Copy request for your admin** action (the distinct-detail pattern `admin_elevation_paused` established). And a non-admin opening an admin package URL (a teammate copied their own address bar) used to dead-end on a generic 403; the error page now resolves the id and offers *"Open {package} →"* to the catalog page, which enforces its own grant check — the bridge reveals nothing the 403-vs-404 split didn't already.

- **The Catalog and the Marketplace browse pages folded into the Library.** `/catalog` and `/marketplace` now 302 into `/library?scope=available` (`?tab=my` arrives at `?scope=mine`), completing the merge the 2026-08-12 design started for `/corporate-memory`, `/apps` and `/stack`: one browse destination, with "things I could add" a **Scope** state of the one list (`All · Yours · Available to add`, replacing the pressed-state "In stack only" toggle) rather than a separate page. The store's richer browse survives inside the Library's kind sections. With the fold, the Library's `+ Add` menu drops its two acquisition rows (`Install from the marketplace`, `Add shared data & recipes` — interim links PR #1276 added so the rail retirement wouldn't strand two live pages) and regroups by **blast radius**: *Create for the workspace* (admin-only: skill · plugin · agent template · data package) vs *Just for you* (upload a file), so the menu no longer mixes "add to me" with "publish to everyone" without a signal. `tests/test_web_nav_user_parity.py` pins the redirects folded-XOR-linked so a retired browse page can be neither stranded nor a redirect loop.

### Added

- **Simulate shows the person's Library, not just the reasons for it.** The Simulate lens answered *why* (membership → grant → tier chains) but never showed the *result* — an admin verifying access still had to imagine the target's screen. A **"What their Library shows"** panel now renders between the chips and the why-chain: per-kind bands (data packages, memory domains) with one row per resource and a state chip in the product's one vocabulary — *In stack · Automatic*, *In stack*, or *Not in stack yet · Optional* — each row linking to the analyst page it predicts (`?from=admin` context carried). Honesty is structural: the new `GET /api/admin/users/{id}/library-preview` computes rows with `StackResolver.browse`, the same grants-based projection the /library page renders from — never `browse_admin`, never a re-derivation from grant rows — so the preview cannot drift from the page it claims to predict, and it reports which membership mode (`auto`/`classic`) it computed under. That mode now also words the older tier chips: under auto-membership an Optional grant reads *"Optional — in their stack"* instead of the classic-mode *"must add it"*, which the new panel would have sat there contradicting. The board could only mint new packages ("One package", "Split by bucket", "+ New package"), but a fresh source's tables often belong in a package analysts already use — a churn table belongs in the existing Customer 360, not in a second bundle beside it. The seed row gains an **"＋ Into existing package…"** picker (loaded on first open, packages already on the board omitted so Finish can't attach twice): picking one adds an **attach-only tray** — name read-only (it belongs to the package), badged *"→ adds to existing"* — and tables moved into it are POSTed to that package on Finish. Nothing is created, the package's sharing stands exactly as it was, and for that reason these trays stay **off the Share step**: a share card there would offer to write a second copy of grants that already exist. The outcome is still said out loud — the finish button counts the two verbs separately ("Create 2 packages · add to 1 existing"), and the Share step notes what was added where even when no new package earned a card. The create drawer always had the "Who gets it" matrix; edit mode hid it, which meant changing *who gets a package* still required the trip to the admin workspace that renaming no longer does. Edit mode now shows the same matrix, hydrated from the grants that exist (`GET /api/admin/grants?resource_type=data_package`) and **diffed on Save** — add is `POST`, a tier change is `PUT /grants/{id}`, an untick is `DELETE` — never written per click, so Cancel stays honest. If the current grants failed to load, Save skips the sharing diff entirely rather than misreading an empty matrix as "revoke everything". With this, name, description, composition *and* audience are all editable from whatever page the drawer opens on (the package's own workspace, the packages grid — which gained a per-card **Edit** — the Tables lens, the Library, and the analyst reading page); the workspace remains the home of what a drawer can't hold: the delivery read-out and per-group people counts.
- **Publishing as the organization happens at create, not as a second moderation step.** `POST /api/store/entities` (and its `from-markdown` sibling) accept `publisher_kind` — `'organization'` is admin-gated server-side (403 `admin_required_for_publisher_kind`), same authority as the existing post-hoc publisher toggle, and the default `'user'` keeps every existing caller exactly where it was. The upload page offers admins a **Publish as** choice (defaulting to *Your organization*), and the `/skills` builder sends the organization mark for admin publishes — so an admin's skills, plugins and agent templates land in colleagues' Libraries carrying the Organization trust mark instead of Community-until-someone-flips-it.
- **One governance cluster on a resource detail page (`detail.manage`), starting with the data package.** Managing the thing a page is showing had grown four different idioms across these pages — an item in the reader's overflow menu on the data package, a bare `edit_icon` on the same page's legacy path, an inline "Edit · admin-only" text link per row on the memory domain, a status-conditional block on the library file — so "can I change this, and where" was answered differently on every page and, on the data package, by a menu entry that navigated to `/admin/tables?edit_package=`: a page about tables. There is now one macro, rendering one labelled block in the rail. Two rules are built into its shape. **Object-scoped only** — every action acts on the thing you are standing on (rename it, change what is in it, change who gets it); instance-scoped work (connect a source, register tables, server config) never appears, and the single `Manage in Admin →` door is the last thing in the block. **It never outranks the reader** — a caller who can manage this arrived to *read* it, so the hero keeps the reading verb ("Add to stack") and the cluster is quiet secondary chrome: a labelled key chip and secondary buttons, no filled accent competing with the hero. It keys on **owner or admin**, since files and collections are owner-owned while store entities have both. On `/catalog/p/{slug}` its "Edit details" opens the same shared drawer `/admin/data-packages/{id}` opens, so a rename happens on the page you are reading rather than three pages away; composition, sharing and the delivery read-out stay behind the Admin door, because those are a governance workspace and this is a reading page. A reader who cannot manage the package is served neither the block nor the editor component behind it.

### Fixed

- **A data package's own page can now edit the data package.** `/admin/data-packages/{id}` is the surface whose whole job is "ONE package, end to end", yet renaming it, re-describing it, re-categorising it or changing its status meant following an *"Edit details…"* link to `/admin/tables?edit_package=` — the Tables lens, a page about something else — where a legacy centred modal did the work. The shared drawer that already owns *creating* a package (`js/components/package_drawer.js`) grew an **edit mode**, so the verb happens on the object you are standing on, exactly as create already does: `open({mode: 'edit', pkgId})` hydrates from `GET /api/admin/data-packages/{id}` and saves through `PUT`. Fields are filled from the API rather than from the row on screen, so a save cannot silently revert someone else's concurrent edit. The mode also owns **what is in the package**: a searchable list of the whole table registry, grouped **project › bucket** — the containers the source systems actually have, where the package is the Agnes one — so "is this package right?" is one question on one surface rather than two. Both group levels carry a tri-state box (all / some / none of their tables), because a package is almost never three arbitrary tables: it is *this bucket*, or *everything from that project*, and a flat list made an admin tick that structure back in one row at a time. Ticking a partly-selected group selects the rest rather than clearing it (`indeterminate` reads as unchecked to `.checked`), a group tick takes only what the current search leaves visible under it, and projects with no source **connection** group under their source's display name rather than a raw `bigquery`/`jira` enum value. Membership is *diffed and applied on Save*, never written per tick — the drawer offers Cancel, and a click that had already hit the API would make that button a lie — and because the metadata write lands first, a table change that fails says so ("The other details were saved") instead of reporting a failed save. A member the registry no longer lists is still rendered, since a row you cannot see is a row you cannot remove. Two things the mode deliberately changes: the **slug is disabled** (it is in the package's URL and in every grant row written against it, and `PUT` carries no slug field — an editable box would discard what was typed, which is why the legacy modal disabled it too), and the **group-access matrix is hidden** (grants on an existing package already exist; a create-shaped matrix would add a second copy of every tier rather than change the ones on the row — sharing is its own editor further down the same page). The table list is edit-only: a package being created has no id yet, so offering it there would collect ticks it could not honour. The legacy modal on `/admin/tables` is untouched and `?edit_package=` still reaches it.
- **Drawer fields that cannot be typed in now look that way.** The shared drawer chrome styled `input`/`textarea` but had no disabled state, so the custom background and near-black ink overrode the browser's own grey-on-grey and a permanently-fixed value read as an editable box. `.ds-drawer__field input[disabled]` now takes the sunken surface, muted ink and a `not-allowed` cursor — it keeps its box and label, because a fixed value still has to be *read*, and only stops looking typeable.

### Internal

- **The Catalog/Marketplace fold's stale-guard debt paid down.** Deleted the two orphaned browse-shell templates (`catalog_unified.html`, `marketplace.html`) and the test files that asserted their markup (`test_web_catalog_unified.py`, `test_web_catalog_reshape.py`, `test_web_stack_card_v56_metadata.py`), removed the dead `_catalog_card_data`/`_catalog_card_memory` adapters (their upload sibling survives — the Artefacts band renders through it), repointed the toolbar/tour guards from the retired `#lib-stack-toggle` to the Scope segment, retired the per-page assertions that read the folded shells (`most_popular` placeholder, marketplace browse CTA/facet, classic memory-grid add-state — each with a pointer to where the surviving behavior is guarded), gave `/marketplace/guide/curated` a reciprocal inbound link from the flea guide (its only door was the deleted browse page), and rewrote `scripts/e2e/smoke_catalog.sh` to smoke the page the redirect actually lands on.

## [0.84.1] - 2026-08-20

### Fixed

- **`/admin/database` backend-migration buttons now confirm before starting a cutover**, instead of firing immediately on click — a real, effectively irreversible backend switch triggered by one stray click. The cloud-Postgres connection-string prompt now also masks its input (`type="password"`) instead of showing the embedded DB password in plaintext, `promptModal` gained an `inputType` option for this. The reserved `duckdb_quack` target no longer shows its raw enum value as the button label — it gets a friendly "coming soon" label and is disabled until the backend supports it. Separately, the "Allowed transitions" reference card no longer sits visibly narrower than the rest of the page on large desktops — it had a stray `max-width: 760px` no sibling card carries.
- **`/admin/server-config` no longer overflows horizontally below ~1200px, and its section sidenav no longer collapses on mobile.** The page's two-column layout (`216px 1fr`) used a bare `1fr` grid track, which never shrinks below its content's min-content width — every viewport narrower than that stayed locked at the desktop width and scrolled sideways instead of reflowing. Fixed with `minmax(0, 1fr)` — the same override `.admin-split` has carried since #1326 plus a mobile breakpoint that stacks the sidenav above the cards. Separately, `.admin-nav`'s own intended mobile hide (`display: none` below 820px) was dead code — an unconditional `display: flex` declared later in the same stylesheet always won over the media query it was meant to override; the media query now runs after it.
- **Five real config sections (`access_policies`, `chat`, `features`, `mcp`, `studio`) were missing from the page's sidenav/title registry.** They rendered with raw snake_case titles in an unlabelled tail group physically below "Danger zone" — so the danger section was never actually last on the page. All five now have proper titles and sit in their matching existing group (General/Integrations/Services).
- **Casing consistency across the admin surface.** `Corporate Memory` → `Corporate memory` (`admin_server_config.html`, the command palette, and its regression test) to match the sentence-case convention used everywhere else; same fix for `Curated Marketplaces`, `Moderation & Trust`, and `Flea Submissions` in the command palette (`_app_scripts.html`), which had drifted from the admin sidebar's own labels for the same pages.
- **The section sidenav's own dropdowns (theme, distribution mode, etc.) now use the app's branded `.ds-dropdown` component** instead of an unstyled native `<select>`. `ds_dropdown.js` only self-initializes at `DOMContentLoaded`, before this page's fields exist (built from an async fetch) — it now also exports `window.dsDropdownInit` for exactly this case.
- **"Test BigQuery/Keboola connection" results now show in the same banner "Save" already used**, instead of a raw colored `<span>` wrapped into the button row.
- **The `.ds-dropdown` component stopped leaking a pair of `document` listeners per dropdown per save.** `init()` attached its Esc and outside-click handlers on `document`, once per host, with no teardown — and `/admin/server-config` rebuilds every section's markup on every save and re-runs the `dsDropdownInit` sweep over it. With a dropdown for each bool and enum leaf across 21 sections that is ~80 new permanent `document` listeners per save, each executing on every subsequent click and pinning the detached DOM it closed over. They no-op behaviourally, so this was degradation and retention rather than incorrectness. Esc and outside-click now live once at module scope and resolve the open menu at event time; `init` registers the host's own closer in a `WeakMap`, so re-initing a rebuilt host is idempotent for the global handlers and the old host becomes collectable.

- **The config page's dropdowns had no accessible name on the default theme.** Each field's `<label for>` points at the native `<select>`, which the `paper` skin sets to `display:none`, so the visible `.ds-dropdown-btn` announced a bare "true" with no indication which setting it belonged to — the exact failure the `dropdown` macro's `aria_label` parameter exists to prevent. `dsDropdownMarkup` now emits the same visually-hidden name span and `aria-labelledby` pair the macro does, and the page ships the per-page markup test every other `.ds-dropdown` conversion in this repo already had.

- **The section sidenav now tracks scroll position** (highlights the section currently in view, not just the last-clicked one) and no longer shows a transient rendering gap above its first row during a fast scroll — `position: sticky` and the list's own internal scroll were combined on one element, which can push the sticky recalculation off the compositor thread on a fast gesture; they're now on two separate elements, matching the pattern the admin-nav column (which never had this issue) already uses.

## [0.84.0] - 2026-08-20

### Added
- **The "Add data source" wizard can now browse a Snowflake account instead of
  asking you to type schema and table names.** `GET /api/admin/data-sources/
  {source_type}/tables` (admin-only, Snowflake today) lists the schemas and
  tables the configured user can see, and the wizard's Snowflake step renders
  them as the same schema-grouped checkbox picker the Keboola step uses —
  filter, select-all and per-schema counts included. Hand-written rows remain
  underneath for anything the listing cannot reach, and a failed listing
  degrades to them instead of blocking the step. Snowflake was the last source
  type whose step was free-text only: nothing validated the strings against the
  account, and because the registry id is composed as `schema + "_" + table`, a
  name pasted with its schema prefix already attached silently produced a
  doubled id (`gold_gold_bi_supply_demand`) pointing at a table that does not
  exist — which then never heals, since only a re-save re-runs the
  remote-extract build. Listing is read-only: it attaches, reads
  `information_schema.tables`, and writes no extract and no registry row. It
  refuses hosts outside `AGNES_REMOTE_ATTACH_HOST_ALLOWLIST` (the same egress
  gate the extract build applies) and answers 502 rather than an empty listing
  when the driver or catalog query fails, so "the account has no tables" is
  never a lie.

### Security

- **A failing Snowflake ATTACH no longer carries the credential in its error.**
  `attach_snowflake` executes a `CREATE OR REPLACE SECRET … (PASSWORD '…')` /
  `PRIVATE_KEY $PK$…$PK$` statement, and DuckDB's parser-class errors quote the
  offending statement back — so on a build whose extension does not recognise one
  of those options, the raised error carried the secret. Every caller then
  forwarded it somewhere durable: a listing 502 and a server log line, and the
  extract build into `sync_state.error`, which the admin registry, `/admin/sync`
  and `agnes admin list-tables` render unredacted. The value is now scrubbed at
  the one place that holds it, so all callers inherit the guarantee — and the
  scrub covers the key-pair arm, which is the one that actually leaks. The
  statement does not embed the stored credential there: it embeds
  `_private_key_pem_and_passphrase(...)`'s output, which normalizes the key to
  an unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM. For a PKCS#1 key, an encrypted key plus
  passphrase, a JSON wrapper or a filesystem path — most real key-pair
  deployments — that PEM is not a substring of the stored token, so scrubbing
  the token alone matched nothing, and the `PRIVATE_KEY $PK$…$PK$` regex needs
  a closing delimiter that a truncated parser echo has already cut off. The
  builder now returns the values it embedded, and the literal patterns have
  unterminated variants, so a whole private key can no longer ride out on a
  truncated error.

### Fixed
- **Catalog preview now works for `query_mode='remote'` tables.** The sample
  endpoint (`GET /api/v2/sample/{id}`, feeding the catalog preview and
  `agnes describe`) refused every non-BigQuery remote row with "never
  materialized — no sample to preview". It now serves a live sample through
  the same analytics view `/api/query` uses (`_remote_attach` re-ATTACH), so
  Snowflake/Keboola/Databricks-with-attach remote rows preview like any other
  table. The mode check also runs before parquet resolution, so a row flipped
  materialized→remote no longer previews its stale leftover parquet. Rows
